chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Abu al-Qasim al-'Alawi narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki, who said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn 'Arafah, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him)

Did Allah create things through His Omnipotence or without it? He replied: It is not permissible to say that Allah created things by means of Omnipotence, because if you say 'He created things by Omnipotence,' it is as if you have made Omnipotence a thing other than Him, and made it a tool with which He created things, and that is polytheism. And if you say 'He created things with Omnipotence,' you are merely describing Him as having the ability and power over them, but He is neither weak nor incapable nor in need of anything else.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali, the compiler of this book, said: When we say that Allah has always been Omnipotent, we intend thereby to negate inability from Him, and we do not intend to affirm a thing co-existing with Him, because He, the Mighty and High, has always been One with nothing co-existing with Him. I will explain the difference between the attributes of Essence and the attributes of Actions in its chapter, if Allah wills.
ai.seo_question: Is Divine Omnipotence a separate entity from God's Essence in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Al-Rida (AS) employs the principle of *Nafi al-Sifat al-Aqliyya* (negation of rational/accidental attributes) to argue that if Divine Power were a distinct entity, it would imply composition and thus polytheism (*Shirk*). This narration underscores the Shia theological stance that God’s attributes are identical with His Essence, distinguishing between His eternal self-sufficiency and the lack of any external instrument or need in His act of creation.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 12. `Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Imran al-Daqqaq (RA) said: Abu al-Qasim al-`Alawi said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma`il al-Barmaki that al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan said: Muhammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Arafah that I asked al-Rida (AS):

“Did Allah create things through His Omnipotence or without it?” Thus, He (AS) replied, You cannot say that Allah created things using His Omnipotence since that would mean that Allah created things by means of His Omnipotence. In so doing, you are saying that His Omnipotence is something other than Him. You are saying that He used His Omnipotence as a tool with which He creates, and that would be polytheism. When you say that Allah has created things using His Omnipotence, it is as if you consider Omnipotence to be separate from Him, and that He obtains His Power over things through it. However, Allah is neither weak nor incapable, nor is He is need of others.

Muhammad ibn `Ali, the Compiler of this book says: When we say that Allah is Omnipotent, we negate any inability from Him. We do not affirm that Omnipotence co-exists along with Him, because He, the Mighty and High, is the One and Only. I will explain the difference between the attributes of essence and attributes of action under the chapter, Allah willing.
